blocks.text: I can form the letters m, n and r.
Your hands and wrists get stronger when you exercise them, just like any other muscle in your body.
Making your hands and wrists stronger helps you to hold your pencil using your tripod grip.

items.title: Playing the piano
items.sub: Hover your hands above pretend piano keys and play a tune with all your fingers.

items.title: Clapping hands
items.sub: Put your hands together and press them hard, so your fingers and palms push against each other.

blocks.text: Practising writing patterns helps us to prepare for writing letters.
Today’s pattern goes **down, up, over and down**, again and again. Try it in the air with your finger and then with your elbow.
Copy and continue the pattern using your tripod grip. Do not lift your pencil while you make the pattern.

items: The letter m is an x-height letter.
The letter m is a small letter.
It does not have an ascender.
The letter m finishes with a flick.

items.def: Letters that reach the middle height on the line.
The line that most letters sit on.

items: 1. Start on the x-height line.
2. Go down to the baseline.
3. Go back up to the x-height line, go over and down.
4. Go back up, go over and down.
5. Finish with a flick.

blocks.text: Do not lift your pencil when you form the letter m.

blocks.q: Which is true about the letter m?
options: It is an x-height letter and it finishes with a flick
blocks.why: The letter m is an x-height letter and finishes with a flick. It is a small letter with no ascender.

blocks.q: Which line does the letter m start on?
blocks.why: The letter m starts on the x-height line and goes down to the baseline.

items: The letter n is an x-height letter.
The letter n is formed in a similar way to the letter m.
They both start at the x-height line, go down, back up, over and down.
They belong to the same letter family.

items.def: Groups of letters that look similar and belong to the same group.

items: 1. Start on the x-height line.
2. Go down to the baseline.
3. Go back up to the x-height line.
4. Go over and down to the baseline.
5. Finish with a flick.

blocks.text: Do not lift your pencil when you form the letter n.

blocks.q: Which letter is the letter n formed in a similar way to?
blocks.why: The letters n and m both start at the x-height line, go down, back up, over and down. They are in the same letter family.

blocks.q: How does the letter n finish?
blocks.why: The letter n goes over, down and finishes with a flick.

items: The letter r is an x-height letter.
The letter r is formed in a similar way to the letters m and n.
They all start on the x-height line, go down to the baseline and go back up and over.
They belong to the same letter family because they are formed in a similar way.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: The letter r does not have an ascender and it does not have a dot at the top.

items: 1. Start on the x-height line.
2. Go down to the baseline.
3. Go back up to the x-height line and go over.
4. Take your pencil off the page.

blocks.text: The letter r finishes by going back up and over.

blocks.q: Which is true about the letter r?
options: It finishes by going back up and over
It has a dot at the top
blocks.why: The letter r is an x-height letter that finishes by going back up and over.

blocks.q: Where does the letter r start?
blocks.why: The letters m, n and r all start on the x-height line.

blocks.q: How does each letter finish? Tap a letter, then tap its column.
columns: Finishes by going back up and over

slides.title: The m, n and r family

blocks.text: The letters m, n and r are all formed by going down, up and over.

items.q: The letters m, n and r are all x-height letters.
The letters m, n and r all start on the x-height line.
The letters m, n and r are all tall letters.

items: The letters m, n and r are all formed by going down, up and over.
They are all x-height letters and all start on the x-height line.
They all go down to the baseline, and back up and over.
The letters m and n finish with a flick.
The letters m, n and r are in the same letter family.

flashcards.front: How are the letters m, n and r formed?
flashcards.back: By going down, up and over.

How does the letter m finish?

flashcards.back: By going back up and over.

flashcards.front: Does the letter m have an ascender?
flashcards.back: No. It is a small letter with no ascender.
Groups of letters that look similar and belong to the same group.

flashcards.front: Why are m, n and r in the same letter family?
flashcards.back: Because they are formed in a similar way: they start on the x-height line, go down to the baseline and go back up and over.
The line that most letters sit on.
Straight, parallel lines that help us write neatly and keep our letters the same size.

flashcards.front: Should you lift your pencil while you form the letter m or n?
flashcards.back: No. Keep your pencil on the paper.
